key_insight: ClinMM-Bench shows that multimodal medical AI can often suggest plausible diagnoses, but reliable multi-turn diagnostic reasoning remains a major challenge.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark better reflects real clinical diagnosis by testing how models update hypotheses as new multimodal information is revealed over time.
method: Built ClinMM-Bench with 1,089 challenging real-world cases and 3,760 medical images across eight specialties.
Evaluated 15 representative MLLMs using a two-level framework covering diagnostic accuracy and reasoning quality.
Analyzed common failure modes, including information synthesis errors, knowledge mapping errors, perception errors, premature closure, and visual hallucination.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, proprietary models achieved the highest overall diagnostic accuracy, but completely correct diagnoses were still limited, and reasoning quality remained constrained.
watch_item: The benchmark highlights that strong single-turn accuracy does not guarantee safe or dependable multi-turn clinical reasoning in real-world use.
paper_title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
